test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 16th November 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: If the diagonal of a square is increased by 4 cm, its area increases by 56 cm² . Find the ratio of the new area of the square to the initial area of the square.
solution:
Area of Square (A₁) = S² ................... (1)

Length of diagonal (d₁) = sqrt{2} S .............. (2)

From eq(2) → S = d₁/sqrt{2}

Area of square (A₁) = (d₁/sqrt{2})²

A₁ = (d₁)²/2 ........... (3)

∴ The diagonal of the square increased by 4cm and its area increased by 56cm².

Increased diagonal of square (d₂) = d₁ + 4 ........... (4)

Increased area of square (A₂) = A₁ + 56 .......... (5)

A₂ = (d₂)²/2

From eq (3) we get, 

A₂ = (d₁ + 4)²/2 .......... (6)

From eq (4) we get,

A₂ - A₁ = 56 .......... (7)

Substitute eq (3) and eq (6) in eq (7)

⇒ (d1 + 4)2/2 - (d1)2/2 = 56

⇒ (d₁ + 4)² - (d1)2 = 56 × 2

⇒ (d1 + 4)2 - (d1)2 = 112

⇒ (d₁)² + 8d₁ + 16 - (d1)2 = 112

⇒ 8d1 + 16 = 112

⇒ 8d1 = 112 - 16

⇒ 8d1 = 96

⇒ d₁ = 12

∴ d₂ = d₁ + 4

d₂ = 12 + 4 = 16

Ratio of the new area of the square to the initial area of the square = A₂ / A₁

A₂ / A₁ = ((d2)2/2) / ((d1)2/2 )

A2 / A₁ = (16² / 2) / (12² / 2)

A2 / A₁ = (256 / 2) / (144 / 2)

A2 / A₁ = 128 / 72

A2 / A₁ = 16 / 9

∴ Here, the Ratio of the new area of the square to the initial area of the square **A₂ : A₁** **= 16 : 9**

Hence, the correct answer is **"16 : 9".**
